# Build book: Guildwork in build order

**Generated** by `tools/plan/plan.py generate` from the component catalog (`docs/design/components/*.toml`) and the work plan (`docs/plan/tasks/*.toml`). Do not edit by hand; rules in [components/README.md](components/README.md).

Part 1 describes the tool stage by stage as it comes into being: which components are added, which grow and which interfaces are ready from which task. Part 2 is the component sheet of each component: what it provides, where it docks and which tasks build it.

## Part 1: Stage by stage

### Stage R: Repo foundation

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`ci-workflows`](#k-ci-workflows) | tool | `.github/workflows/` | The workflow set of the product repo: ci.yml with the job split ts, tools, security and ci-ok as the only required check, CodeQL, Scorecard, daily full scans of main (vulnerabilities and ScanCode), Renovate configuration and the measurement of waiting time and concurrency. Not the release, portability and acceptance workflows of later stages and not the deny jobs (denylist-scanner). |
| [`core`](#k-core) | package | `packages/core/` | Base types for every package: result and error types with problem+json, IDs and canonical JSON, clock and randomness, SecretValue, logger with redaction, metric and trace facade with catalog and the single source of redaction rules. Without workspace dependencies and without the OTel SDK (telemetry starts that). |
| [`denylist-scanner`](#k-denylist-scanner) | tool | `tools/denylist/` | Finds references to companies, persons and hosts, private networks and home paths in tree, history, commits, identities and PR texts, without ever printing a term or the matching text; runs locally, in the CI and before publication. Not the text rules for language and dashes (hooks-und-textpruefung). |
| [`hooks-und-textpruefung`](#k-hooks-und-textpruefung) | tool | `tools/hooks/` | Checks texts (no dashes, English in public docs, glossary, instance data), links and anchors, commit messages with DCO and Plan-Task, and requires a Red Team report before the push; plus the hooks and the quality docs. Not the deny list scanner and not the secret search. |
| [`lizenz-gate`](#k-lizenz-gate) | tool | `tools/ci/license_check.py` | Keeps the license situation of the repo verifiable: LICENSE checksum, SPDX headers, licenses of all dependencies against the allowlist, license texts, ADR-39 counter-test in the lockfile, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, ScanCode before release; plus the verified license list of the tools. Not the license gate of the images (release-werkzeuge, 0-E21). |
| [`opengrep-regeln`](#k-opengrep-regeln) | tool | `.opengrep/` | Own Opengrep rules under Apache-2.0 with rule tests that enforce code rules within packages (write subpath of the plugins only in the executors of the Effect Gateway, no model credentials from the environment, process.env only in loader modules, no direct clock, no foreign content in the log). From 0-E09-T05 additionally the rule single write path for calls of write methods (00 FE-054, 04 FE-445; the type-aware test from 04 FE-439 is dropped). Not the analyzer plugin for customer repos (plugin-analyzer-opengrep). |
| [`plan-werkzeug`](#k-plan-werkzeug) | tool | `tools/plan/` | Checks and generates the work plan in the product repo (English TOML keys) together with the component catalog, so that the team works through the plan there. Not the contents of the plan (produkt-doku) and not the synchronization with issues. |
| [`produkt-doku`](#k-produkt-doku) | delivery | `docs/` | The public English documentation in the product repo: architecture, ADRs as MADR, owner decisions without quotes, detailed design, plan and untranslated research with a header. After V10 the only source; the German files in the ops repo are frozen. |
| [`prozess-repo-und-erster-push`](#k-prozess-repo-und-erster-push) | process | `-` | The steps at the hoster that only the owner carries out or approves: create repos and organization, push the root commit and make it public, set up ruleset, environments and Renovate app, probe PRs and stage report R. No code. |
| [`prozess-veroeffentlichung`](#k-prozess-veroeffentlichung) | process | `-` | Turns the German planning files into a neutral English version, checks it with the items V1 to V9 and produces exactly one signed root commit with evidence. Tools live in the ops repo under publish/, never in the product repo. |
| [`repo-einstellungen-pruefung`](#k-repo-einstellungen-pruefung) | tool | `tools/ci/check_settings.py` | Records the target values of the repo settings (ruleset, environments, variables, security, SHA pinning) in machine-readable form and compares them read-only with the actual state at the hoster. Sets no setting itself; the owner does that. |
| [`repo-geruest-und-toolchain`](#k-repo-geruest-und-toolchain) | tool | `./` | The scaffold on which every task builds: required and community files, package template, TypeScript and Python toolchain, verified binary download, Makefile with gates.toml as the only gate list and the local dry run of the workflows. Not the individual check tools (own components). |
| [`schichtenpruefung`](#k-schichtenpruefung) | tool | `tools/ci/check_layers.py` | Enforces the allowed dependencies between workspace packages from quality/layers.toml (package.json, imports, testkit only in tests, freedom from cycles) and creates new packages only via the generator. Checks no rules within a package (Opengrep does that) and no external licenses (license gate). |
| [`sicherheits-scans`](#k-sicherheits-scans) | tool | `.gitleaks.toml` | Finds secrets in the history (gitleaks with a rule for Anthropic credentials and exact test values) and known vulnerabilities in the lockfiles, in the PR only newly introduced ones. Not the analyzer plugins for customer repos. |
| [`workflow-policy`](#k-workflow-policy) | tool | `tools/ci/check_workflows.py` | Checks every GitHub workflow against the policy of the repo (runners, SHA pins, rights, triggers, expressions, concurrency, job count) and runs actionlint and zizmor. Not workflow-guard (stage 2), which checks foreign repos. |

### Stage 0: Foundation and installability

Builds on stage R.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`abnahme-werkzeug`](#k-abnahme-werkzeug) | tool | `tools/acceptance/` | Acceptance matrix per stage as TOML with the check tool check.py, which proves each named test and its green state on main, and a collective run of the contract suites with a report (FE-635); builds no suite and no test itself. |
| [`admin-api`](#k-admin-api) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/admin/` | Framework of the admin API under /admin/api/v1 (session, CSRF, role guard, Problem Details, audit per change, route registration for all areas), OIDC login, emergency admin with TOTP and the framework of the internal commands; not the domain endpoints (those are provided by ui-setup-assistent, ui-betrieb, `ui-run-record`, `not-aus` and other areas). |
| [`admin-ui`](#k-admin-ui) | program | `apps/admin-ui/` | React SPA with Vite under /admin/: router, layout, page registry, typed client of the admin API, login and break-glass pages, delivery by the role web with CSP and shared markers (ADR-47, condition 8); the domain pages are delivered by ui-setup-assistent, ui-betrieb, ui-run-record, not-aus and later areas. |
| [`alarm-automat`](#k-alarm-automat) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/alerts/` | Computes the required alerts itself in the role orchestrator from stored facts, keeps their state in the table alerts, delivers them via log, webhook and later notifier and shows them in the admin API. No third-party alarm backend; rules of other areas dock on via the rule list. |
| [`audit-kette`](#k-audit-kette) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/audit/` | Tamper-evident trail of the installation: writes every audit entry into a hash chain within the transaction of the domain change, checks chain and anchors and anchors the head daily outside the database. Not here: tables, triggers and the functions audit_head and audit_insert (migration in area 01) and the redaction rules (core). |
| [`backup-restore`](#k-backup-restore) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/ops/` | Role ops in the image control-plane with backup schedule, automatic restore test into a throwaway database and the commands guildwork backup and restore including PITR evidence; not the table backup_runs (DDL in 01, migration from 0-E02) and not the profiles s3 and pitr (compose-buendel). |
| [`betreiber-doku`](#k-betreiber-doku) | delivery | `docs/ops/` | Operator docs under docs/ops (installation, operations, Hetzner, Azure, air gap, storage, upgrade, backup) with executable command blocks and the check tool doc_commands_check.py, plus the measured hardware start values in the schema; not the product docs for users (produkt-doku, area 00). |
| [`claude-code-startwege`](#k-claude-code-startwege) | plugin | `plugins/claude-code/src/launch/` | Builds the hardened invocation of claude per credential kind as a pure function: argv, environment only from the allowlist, managed settings, MCP configuration, empty configuration directory, prompt files; plus the host file of the subscription token with expiry warning and from stage 8 the cloud credential kinds (files under src/credentials/). Starts no process itself (run does that) and never holds a real API key (it lives only in the relay). |
| [`cli`](#k-cli) | program | `apps/cli/` | Command guildwork as a Node SEA binary with a shared scaffold (options, output, error codes, Compose wrapper, bundle and digest check) and the commands upgrade, worker register, github-app create, admin break-glass, config validate and version; install and doctor are separate components (cli-install, cli-doctor), backup and restore belong to backup-restore. |
| [`cli-doctor`](#k-cli-doctor) | role | `apps/cli/src/doctor/` | Command guildwork doctor: framework with check registry, the installation checks D01 to D34 and the per-repo checks R01 to R04 (FE-642); only checks and writes nothing except probe objects, which it deletes, and the report. It calls the check functions of other areas (separation, audit anchor, blueprint, agent_ci) but does not build them. |
| [`cli-install`](#k-cli-install) | role | `apps/cli/src/commands/install.ts` | Command guildwork install: preflight without writing, bundle and signature check, only add to the target folder, pull by digest, migrate, start, one-time code of the emergency admin only on stdout, doctor; with an air gap branch and the test environment tools/airgap-env. Not upgrade (cli) and not the checks themselves (cli-doctor). |
| [`compose-buendel`](#k-compose-buendel) | delivery | `deploy/compose/` | The Compose bundle that the installer writes into the target folder: services, networks according to ADR-62, volumes, healthchecks, Caddy routes, profiles s3, pitr, observability and kb-vectors, fragment rule and host-prepare.sh; not the installer logic (cli-install), not the programs in the services and not the fragment observability.compose.yaml (telemetry). |
| [`config-installation`](#k-config-installation) | package | `packages/config/src/installation/` | Reads installation.yaml once at the start of every role, checks it strictly (YAML 1.2, unknown keys, driver keys, cross-checks), freezes it and publishes the schema and the reference of the default values. Never resolves secrets and is not the resolver of the org, repo group and repo layers (config-resolver). |
| [`config-resolver`](#k-config-resolver) | package | `packages/config/` | Provides the effective configuration of a run: schemas with x-merge and x-qualification, loading of the org, group and repo files at the pinned SHA, merging only in the stricter direction, fail closed, consistency rules, snapshot with qualification_key per service, expression language and repo_overrides. Not here: the loader of installation.yaml (config-installation), the profile and key themselves (qualifikationsprofil) and the resolver rules of the plugin areas (config-resolver-regeln). |
| [`config-resolver-regeln`](#k-config-resolver-regeln) | package | `packages/config/src/rules/` | Pure check rules that the config resolver calls when loading the effective configuration and the orchestrator calls at claim time; each rule rejects only the affected runtime, the service or the run, never the installation. The resolver itself, the hierarchy and the JSON Schema are built by config-resolver and config-installation; this component provides the rules and their schema additions. |
| [`container-images`](#k-container-images) | delivery | `deploy/images/` | Builds all OCI images of the platform for amd64 and arm64 by digest, without root, with healthcheck, labels and license gate, including the workflow images.yml; provides the four core images and the shared tool images, not the images that their introducing component provides itself (registry-cache, mermaid-check, embedder, engines; table in 06 section 2.2); not the programs in the images and not the release (release-werkzeuge). |
| [`contract-harness`](#k-contract-harness) | package | `packages/testkit/src/contract/` | Checks every plugin and every driver against its contract with recorded real responses: cassette format, strict replay without network, recording without external effect, redaction, attestation and the abstract suites per kind with reference fakes. Not here: the implementations of the plugins and drivers and the load check at runtime (plugin-rahmen). |
| [`contracts`](#k-contracts) | package | `packages/contracts/` | The only source of the types and schemas through which core, plugins, drivers and services talk to each other: base types, the eight binding contracts v1alpha1, sketches, plugin and service manifest with validation and later the binding contracts Analyzer and WorkItemProvider. Contains no network or database access; loader and transport are in plugin-rahmen, the event schema in event-schema, the harness in testkit. |
| [`control-plane`](#k-control-plane) | program | `apps/control-plane/` | One program for all roles of the control plane: selects the roles from the argument, starts HTTP (web) and pg-boss workers (orchestrator), mounts the areas via WebMount and reports readiness. Contains no domain logic itself; ingress, router, orchestrator, policy and ledger are separate components, the role ops belongs to detailed design 06. |
| [`control-plane-ingress`](#k-control-plane-ingress) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/ingress/` | Accepts webhooks, relays and ci_event per plugin instance, checks the signature on the raw body before any parsing, puts raw data into the BlobStore and the inbox, normalizes asynchronously into events with dedupe and catches up via reconcile and poll. Decides nothing about routes, permissions or runs; the router does that. |
| [`control-plane-orchestrator`](#k-control-plane-orchestrator) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/orchestrator/` | Drives every run according to the run state machine (one JSON file as the only source): intake with object lock and reservation, transitions in one transaction, steps via the service controllers, control commands, deadlines, status comment, lifting on upgrade, plus the list and registration of all queues. Decides no policy and no budget itself and never writes past the Effect Gateway. |
| [`control-plane-router`](#k-control-plane-router) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/router/` | Assigns every new event to a route: cheap filters, repo assignment, fresh re-read against TOCTOU, configuration at the base SHA, route selection with deny by default and permission check G0 at the provider; the result is a RouteDecision or a skipped event. Creates no run and knows no object lock (FE-210); later stages only add routes, arguments and permission forms here. |
| [`credential-broker`](#k-credential-broker) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/broker/` | Issues short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials: secrets from the SecretStore with audit, SCM tokens per effect or per clone with exactly one repo and profile, item tokens, LLM grants per item and pool keys; publishes the JWKS of its own issuer. Never stores a token and never sees a subscription token; the key ring itself lives in the driver identity-self-issuer. |
| [`credential-relay`](#k-credential-relay) | role | `apps/egress-proxy/src/relay/` | Holds the LLM credential of an item only in the memory of the egress proxy (Z1), accepts from the sandbox only model calls with the placeholder, checks them against the rules R1 to R10, sets the real header or the SigV4 signature and counts the usage. Does not book into the ledger itself and does not apply to the start path subscription. |
| [`db`](#k-db) | package | `packages/db/` | Sole access of the control plane and the eval service to Postgres: connection per role, tenant context with row-level security, installation scope with a fixed list of callers, Kysely types, thin repositories and the maintenance jobs for partitions and retention. Not here: domain logic, state transitions and audit chain (belong to the users or to 04), migrator and migration files 0001 to 0008 (db-migrator, db-schema-kern), queues (db-queue). |
| [`db-migrator`](#k-db-migrator) | package | `packages/db/src/migrator/` | Applies the numbered SQL migrations forward only (lock against parallel runs, checksums, backup gate, halt points, minimum versions of PostgreSQL and pgvector) and checks at the start of each role whether schema and release match. Not here: content of the migrations (db-schema-kern and the areas), linter (migration-lint), flow of guildwork upgrade (CLI). |
| [`db-queue`](#k-db-queue) | package | `packages/db/src/queue/` | Encapsulates pg-boss behind QueueRuntime and sendInTx, so that jobs are created in the same transaction as their DB change and the unverified option names stay in one place. Knows no queue names and no handlers; the list of queues and the registration live in the orchestrator. |
| [`db-schema-kern`](#k-db-schema-kern) | package | `packages/db/migrations/` | SQL migrations 0001 to 0008 with the core tables of stage 0 (DDL, constraints, indexes, partitioning, append-only protection of the audit) and tenant separation via row-level security. Not here: tables of individual areas and later stages (table directory, each its own migration of the building task), maintenance functions 0009 (db), domain logic of the writers. |
| [`driver-blob-fs`](#k-driver-blob-fs) | driver | `drivers/blob-fs/` | BlobStore on a local directory for single-host and tests: atomic writes, etag as SHA-256, list with cursor. Without PRESIGN, VERSIONING, OBJECT_LOCK and SSE_KMS; retainUntil is rejected so that nobody assumes Object Lock (FE-416), therefore no sink for the daily anchor. |
| [`driver-blob-s3`](#k-driver-blob-s3) | driver | `drivers/blob-s3/` | BlobStore via the S3 API for SeaweedFS, Garage and S3-compatible services, with capabilities by probe (versioning, Object Lock, presign) and retainUntil via COMPLIANCE as sink for the daily anchor. No MinIO (ADR-43); Azure Blob and GCS are separate drivers. |
| [`driver-identity-self-issuer`](#k-driver-identity-self-issuer) | driver | `drivers/identity-self-issuer/` | Own OIDC issuer of the installation: key ring ES256 with next, active, retired in the SecretStore (FE-410, FE-411, FE-427) and ambientToken for federation targets. No exchange for foreign credentials in stage 0 (exchange yields unsupported, FE-424); the HTTP endpoints are provided by the credential broker. |
| [`driver-secret-env`](#k-driver-secret-env) | driver | `drivers/secret-env/` | SecretStore via environment variables with a fixed name mapping (FE-415), read-only. Without WRITE: no automatic key rotation, put yields unsupported. |
| [`driver-secret-file`](#k-driver-secret-file) | driver | `drivers/secret-file/` | SecretStore in files, each secret with versions, AES-256-GCM with a separate master key (FE-414), with WRITE and thus automatic key rotation. No SIGN: signing keys are read into the memory of the control plane for signing. |
| [`dummy-service`](#k-dummy-service) | service | `services/dummy/` | Service without domain logic and without an LLM (default) that proves the whole chain of stage 0 from the comment to the effect in mode record, with a harness mode against a fake upstream, the end-to-end tests of the failure paths and the probe run of the assistant; never live (policy dummy.never_live). |
| [`effect-gateway`](#k-effect-gateway) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/effects/` | Sole write path to the outside: accepts write requests and platform effects, checks schema, target, policy, content and the checkers of later stages, assigns the idempotency key, keeps the outbox in effects and dispatches via the executors with retry and reconciliation. Calls no write method of a plugin itself (only the executors do that) and decides no policy rule POL-* (the policy engine does that). |
| [`effekt-executoren`](#k-effekt-executoren) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/effects/executors/` | Exactly one executor per effect type, which calls the write method of the plugin with the token per effect, sets the marker, reconciles after a crash and selects the fallback level; only here may write methods of the plugins be called. Not here: acceptance, policy, retry and ordering (effect gateway) and the plugin methods themselves (plugins). |
| [`egress-proxy`](#k-egress-proxy) | program | `apps/egress-proxy/` | Sole way of a sandbox to the outside: CONNECT only to exactly allowed hosts per item, binding to the item via the network interface, DNS only in the proxy, air gap as intersection, connection log per item; controlled by the worker via a control API. No TLS interception except in the inspection proxy, no database connection. |
| [`eval-adapter-harbor`](#k-eval-adapter-harbor) | eval | `eval/adapters/harbor/` | Maps tasks in the Harbor format to a ticket fixture with image by digest, fetches the patch from the eval log and checks it in the locked protocol in a fresh sandbox with the task's verifier. Not for the selection of the coder sets (stage 2) and not for scoring across several tasks. |
| [`eval-adapter-reviewbench`](#k-eval-adapter-reviewbench) | eval | `eval/adapters/reviewbench/` | Maps review cases (repo at head, base, diff) to a PR fixture of a platform run and translates recorded inline findings into findings.json per the ReviewBench container contract; serves R2, R4, R5 and own review sets. Not for scoring (scorers of the sets) and not for the reviewer-specific adapter from stage 1. |
| [`eval-core`](#k-eval-core) | eval | `eval/core/` | Pure types, TypeBox schemas and contracts of the eval package without IO (set and case format, label and reference lines, adapter and scorer contract, reference values, eval report, reference qualification), shared by runner, control plane and all sets. Not for statistics, gates and judges (separate components in the same package) and not for run control or database access. |
| [`eval-dienst`](#k-eval-dienst) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/eval/` | Server-side part of the eval in the control plane: eval tables, admission per case (origin, license, data path ADR-70), run and case state machine with platform runs in mode record, judge calls, scoring via eval-core and the eval API. Not for matrix, mode decision and adoption (eval-qualifikation) and not for statistics (eval-statistik). |
| [`eval-fixture-provider`](#k-eval-fixture-provider) | plugin | `plugins/eval-fixture/` | Built-in plugin that supplies case runs of an eval run with read-only SCM and ticket responses from the prepared fixtures (PR at head, diff, ticket text), so that an eval run never reaches a real SCM or ticket endpoint (FE-748). Not for write paths (effects land in the eval log of the effect gateway) and not for tests of other areas (testkit fixture-server serves that). |
| [`eval-gates`](#k-eval-gates) | eval | `eval/core/src/gates/` | Gate A and gate B per service as a data file with source anchor in 10, load check, status combination across judges and parts and rules_hash; plus the first gate file of the reviewer. Not for the statistics per part (eval-statistik) and not for the matrix or the mode decision (eval-qualifikation). |
| [`eval-qualifikation`](#k-eval-qualifikation) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/eval/matrix.ts` | Qualification matrix per qualification_key and scope with validity computed on every query, mode decision off, shadow, live including the marking default not proven, merge gate condition, adoption of the reference qualification with remeasurement in shadow and online decay (matrix.ts, reference.ts). Not for the measurement itself (eval service), the export of the file (eval-runner) or the profile (qualifikationsprofil). |
| [`eval-querschnitts-suites`](#k-eval-querschnitts-suites) | eval | `eval/suites/` | Framework of the cross-cutting suites S1 to S8 (defineSuiteCase, catalog with required cases per stage, lint, run with stage filter, suite report, probes on the real artifact) and the cases of all stages that areas contribute to it (FE-720, FE-736). Not for the eval sets of the services (gate A, gate B) and not for unit or contract tests without catalog ID. |
| [`eval-richter`](#k-eval-richter) | eval | `eval/core/src/judges/` | Judge specification as versioned files, choice of an own judge of a different family, calibration against human labels with kappa and age warning. Not for the judge calls themselves (ModelProvider path or work item, in the eval service) and not for individual judge prompts of a set. |
| [`eval-runner`](#k-eval-runner) | eval | `eval/runner/` | Command guildwork-eval as a client without own permissions: check sets, load and check pinned sources, prepare cases and start and query runs via the eval API, calibrate, label, export the reference qualification; plus the check tool against third-party data in the repo. Not for admission, run state machine or matrix (server-side in the eval service, FE-700) and not for the installer command guildwork (FE-730). |
| [`eval-saetze-reviewer`](#k-eval-saetze-reviewer) | eval | `eval/sets/` | The eval sets of the reviewer as declarative pins with checksums (R2, R4, R5), own references and human labels (R1), the scorers per set, the judge prompt review-match and the read-off reference values; stage 0 builds pins, the scorers martian, reviewbench, swe-prbench, aacr, label schema and the first labeling round, stage 1 the scorer own-review, the calibration and the first real runs. Not for adapters, statistics or gate files and never for copies of third-party data (FE-728). |
| [`eval-statistik`](#k-eval-statistik) | eval | `eval/core/src/stats/` | Pure, deterministic statistics of all eval measurements: metrics with the mean over repetitions, seedable randomness, cluster bootstrap, kappa, decision per part (green, red, not decidable), sample size and upper bound at zero failures. Not for gate files, status combination or storage. |
| [`event-schema`](#k-event-schema) | package | `packages/contracts/src/events/` | The only definition of the normalized event (TriggerEvent through StoredEvent) together with the pure functions that TriggerSources, ingress and router need in common: command parser, dedupe key, routing name and object key (FE-501). Not here: ingress, inbox and router themselves (detailed design 02) and internal events of the orchestrator such as item.triaged. |
| [`limit-ledger`](#k-limit-ledger) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/ledger/` | Hard limit for costs, runs, tokens and parallelism: key chain and buckets from the snapshot, atomic reservation across all keys before the run, booking of cumulative usage during the run with abort, settlement and release afterwards. Does not start or end runs itself; it reports budget_exhausted to the orchestrator. |
| [`migration-lint`](#k-migration-lint) | tool | `tools/migration-lint/` | Static check of all migration files against the expand/contract rules and forbidden statements as a gate in make check, plus the probe that code of N-1 runs against the schema after an expand migration. Not here: applying the migrations (db-migrator) and the full upgrade test S8 (0-E21). |
| [`plattform-mcp`](#k-plattform-mcp) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/mcp/` | MCP server of the control plane through which a harness in the sandbox reads fresh context with its item token and submits write requests; every call is checked against token, lease and service manifest. Applies no effect itself (that is done by the Effect Gateway) and calls no model. |
| [`plugin-claude-code`](#k-plugin-claude-code) | plugin | `plugins/claude-code/` | AgentRuntime for the unmodified Claude Code CLI in the worker: installs the pinned harness with checksum into the sandbox, starts it via the hardened start path, translates the NDJSON stream into RuntimeEvents without plaintext and delivers AgentRunResult with usage, cost and limits; from stage 2 resume and steer. The start path per credential kind is in claude-code-startwege; the worker provides sandbox, relay and snapshot. |
| [`plugin-exec-docker`](#k-plugin-exec-docker) | plugin | `plugins/exec-docker/` | Implements the ExecutionBackend contract for Docker with sysbox or gvisor isolation: item network, volumes, hardened container without resolver, exec, copyIn, copyOut, exportBundle and complete destroy, all via the socket proxy. No snapshot, no dispatch and no weaker isolation as a fallback. |
| [`plugin-github`](#k-plugin-github) | plugin | `plugins/github/` | Shared part of the two GitHub packages github (TriggerSource, SCMProvider) and github-issues (WorkItemProvider): manifests, instance configuration, own REST and GraphQL client on ctx.http, app JWT, token per permission profile, app creation via manifest flow and the recorded contract fixtures. Runs only in the control plane (FE-515); trigger, SCM methods and issues are in separate components. |
| [`plugin-github-issues`](#k-plugin-github-issues) | plugin | `plugins/github/src/issues/` | WorkItemProvider github-issues: read GitHub Issues as tickets (router, platform MCP) and, per stage, the write methods that an Effect Gateway executor needs first. Uses the token of the linked scm instance via the broker; Jira and other ticket systems are separate plugins. |
| [`plugin-github-scm`](#k-plugin-github-scm) | plugin | `plugins/github/src/scm/` | Maps the SCMProvider contract to the GitHub API: read methods for control plane, platform MCP and services, write methods only for the Effect Gateway with a token per effect, push via Git bundle without force, and the optional methods of the later stages. Decides nothing itself: policy, push check and retry lie with the caller; plugin-github mints the token. |
| [`plugin-github-trigger`](#k-plugin-github-trigger) | plugin | `plugins/github/src/trigger/` | Turns GitHub webhooks and reconcile or poll runs into normalized TriggerEvents with a stable dedupeKey and writes the acknowledgment as an effect. Not here: accepting the HTTP call, inbox, dedupe and routing (ingress and router of the control plane) and storing the cursor (caller). |
| [`plugin-model-anthropic`](#k-plugin-model-anthropic) | plugin | `plugins/model-anthropic/` | ModelProvider anthropic-api for single calls (gate, verifier, judge) in the worker as work item model_call, via the credential relay with a placeholder per item and the Vercel AI SDK, with cost from a versioned price table (from 8-E06-T01 only the control plane calculates cost). Not for agent runs (AgentRuntime) and never from the control plane (FE-531); no embeddings. |
| [`plugin-model-claude-cli`](#k-plugin-model-claude-cli) | plugin | `plugins/model-claude-cli/` | ModelProvider claude-cli for required single calls in the personal operator mode: starts claude -p per call with the start path subscription in a sandbox of the item, without tools and without MCP, with schema output and an audited fallback level (ADR-58). Not for tool calls (tools yields unsupported) and without cost in USD. |
| [`plugin-rahmen`](#k-plugin-rahmen) | package | `packages/contracts/src/host/` | Loads built-in plugin and driver packages per instance with the load conditions 1 to 15, runs the state machine of the instance, decides on capabilities and fallback levels, retries calls at the caller and wraps every plugin with time limit, error encapsulation and write protection. Persists nothing itself (the control plane writes plugin_instances) and starts no subprocess plugins in stage 0 (FE-536). |
| [`policy-engine`](#k-policy-engine) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/policy/` | Pure function over stored facts that decides run start, service mode, write requests, platform effects and work items with rule IDs POL-nnn and logs every decision in policy_decisions. Never reads model text and executes nothing; the Effect Gateway executes effects, and the citation check itself lives there. |
| [`portabilitaetstest`](#k-portabilitaetstest) | tool | `tools/portability/` | Reusable workflow portability.yml with scripts that installs, checks, upgrades, backs up and restores every release candidate on fresh runners (amd64, arm64; gVisor, Sysbox) using only documented commands, plus air gap, telemetry default and PITR; only checks, delivers nothing. |
| [`produkt-telemetrie`](#k-produkt-telemetrie) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/telemetry/` | Product telemetry with opt-in (endpoints and page /admin/telemetry), preview according to a fixed schema and sending only to telemetry.endpoint, update notice via the Releases API (the capture sink for tests is provided by the testkit); not the version age (ui-betrieb); no receiver run by the project (FE-617) and not the operational telemetry (OpenTelemetry, area 00). |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-0`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-0) | process | `-` | Work without own code to complete stage 0: the owner clarifies the public, free registry, approves the first signed release v0.1.0, and the stage report proves every done criterion from 08 with check.py; release and registry have an external effect and run only with the owner's go. |
| [`prozess-eval-konten-und-lizenzen`](#k-prozess-eval-konten-und-lizenzen) | process | `-` | Work without own code that only the owner can decide or carry out: the subscription token of the project installation for eval and reference qualification (owner decision O28: only Claude via the subscription, no third-party account, no API key), license requests for datasets of later stages; the agent delivers one decision sheet or one guide each and carries out nothing with an external effect. Not for reading baseline values from public pages except as preparation of a decision. |
| [`qualifikationsprofil`](#k-qualifikationsprofil) | package | `packages/config/src/qualification/` | Canonical qualification profile of a service (ADR-66) from the effective configuration, the installation and the contribution of the service, from which qualification_key (qk1-) and the variant without credential_kind (qx1-) are derived; one source for resolver, policy, eval and merge gate. Not for the matrix, the gates or storing in the snapshot (resolver). |
| [`release-werkzeuge`](#k-release-werkzeuge) | tool | `tools/release/` | Tools and workflow of the release: release.json according to ReleaseManifest, bundle and SHA256SUMS, image license gate with counter-test and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, list of third-party components and release.yml with digest, Trivy, SBOM, signature, attestation and tag; does not trigger a release itself (owner go in prozess-abnahme-stufe-0). |
| [`sdk-service`](#k-sdk-service) | package | `packages/sdk-service/` | The only interface of the services to the platform: service definition, controller contract with the host of the control plane, job handler with context in the worker, reading of the envelope inputs and platform MCP client. Only types, ports and helpers; the ports are implemented by the control plane and the worker. |
| [`socket-proxy`](#k-socket-proxy) | role | `apps/worker/src/socket-proxy/` | Sole holder of the Docker daemon socket on single-host: passes through to the worker only the Docker API calls that a sandbox needs, and checks on creation runtime, image digest, network, mounts, rights and label. Replaces no kernel boundary and knows no work items. |
| [`telemetry`](#k-telemetry) | package | `packages/telemetry/` | Starts the OTel SDK in each role before other code, registers the metrics of the catalog with cardinality protection, gives the harness the OTel environment and delivers the collector as a Compose fragment. Only apps use it; packages measure via the facade in core. Not the product telemetry (produkt-telemetrie). |
| [`testkit`](#k-testkit) | package | `packages/testkit/` | Shared test helpers of all areas: real Postgres per test file, controllable clock and randomness, log capture, secret check, HTTP replay with network block and the fakes and check helpers that tests of several areas need. Only in test files; contract harness and E2E stack in the same package are separate components. Building blocks whose signature another area defines (test IdP, fake Anthropic, telemetry sink, Azure recorder from 06 section 2.17, expectRecordedEffects from 04 section 2.1.6) are built by testkit as well, but they are offered there (00 FE-060). |
| [`testkit-e2e-stack`](#k-testkit-e2e-stack) | package | `packages/testkit/src/e2e/` | Test building block for end-to-end tests of the chain: Postgres as a test container, roles of the control plane in the test process, real worker with gVisor, egress proxy and fixture server with recorded GitHub responses, plus the fixture server as a container for smoke and air-gap runs; never runs in an installation. |
| [`treiber-lader`](#k-treiber-lader) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/drivers/` | Loads from installation.yaml exactly one BlobStore, one SecretStore and the list CloudIdentity, only with a passed contract suite, determines the capabilities by probe and polls health() every 60 s. | [`ui-betrieb`](#k-ui-betrieb) | ui | `apps/admin-ui/src/pages/` | Read-only operations views with their admin endpoints: status with version age and audit anchor, pools with checked capabilities, services with qualification, audit with chain status, costs from the ledger and the alerts page; not the alert API itself (alarm-automat, area 00), not the telemetry opt-ins (produkt-telemetrie) and not Run Record or kill switch. |
| [`ui-setup-assistent`](#k-ui-setup-assistent) | ui | `apps/admin-ui/src/pages/Setup/` | Setup wizard as a state machine per installation with endpoints, pages and the overlay installation_settings (file wins, FE-614): emergency admin, SSO, GitHub App via manifest, model access, first pool, probe run with the dummy; not the telemetry opt-ins (ui-betrieb) and not the resolver (02). |
| [`work-api`](#k-work-api) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/work/` | The only way work gets from the control plane to workers and results come back: create and revoke work items, claim with capability matching, leases with heartbeat, results, artifact upload and drain. Does not decide on run states (orchestrator), budgets (ledger) or write requests (Effect Gateway). |
| [`work-item-umschlag`](#k-work-item-umschlag) | package | `packages/contracts/src/work/` | Versioned TypeBox schemas including types for everything that travels between control plane and worker: envelope, grants, result, error and Work API messages. The write request schemas (ProposalV1) are offered by the Effect Gateway (FE-345). No logic, no storage location and no check of rights; the envelope never carries a secret. |
| [`worker`](#k-worker) | program | `apps/worker/` | Program guildwork-worker on the worker host (Z1): fetches work items only outbound via the Work API, checks its capabilities itself, clones in Z1, runs each item in a fresh sandbox and always destroys it. Holds no database connection, calls no model itself and decides no write requests. |
| [`worker-harness-umgebung`](#k-worker-harness-umgebung) | role | `apps/worker/src/harness/` | Builds in the worker the environment of the harness process from an empty environment and an allowlist per credential kind, reads the subscription token per item from the host file of the operator and gives the runtime the harness cache directory of the worker host (copied in via copyIn, FE-333). Does not start the harness itself (that is done by the runtime plugin via the item lifecycle) and stores no credential. |
| [`worker-paket`](#k-worker-paket) | delivery | `deploy/worker-package/` | Package for workers on own hardware: compose.worker.yaml with worker, socket-proxy and egress-proxy, systemd unit and README with upgrade path; never contains a pool key, the operator places it themselves after guildwork worker register. |

### Stage 1: Reviewer core, GitHub, local Claude Code

Builds on stage 0.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`eval-adapter-reviewer`](#k-eval-adapter-reviewer) | eval | `eval/adapters/reviewbench/src/reviewer/` | Reviewer part of collect in the adapter reviewbench from 07 (FE-853): reads the ReviewArtifact of the case run via a narrow read view and returns all visible findings (inline and summary, FE-824) as findings.json, plus the prompt eval/bare-prompts/reviewer.md and the mapping of the output of the bare arm (eval-bare) for gate A. No own package, no prepare, no sets and no scoring (adapters, sets and scorers from 07 do that). |
| [`guidelines`](#k-guidelines) | package | `packages/guidelines/` | Loads guidelines and rule files only at the base SHA and selects them per path with a budget and a stable rule ID; in stage 1 as the export ./guidelines of @guildwork/service-reviewer under services/reviewer/src/guidelines/, from stage 7 as the package @guildwork/guidelines with all formats. Does not evaluate rules (that is done by the finder standards and the standards service). |
| [`not-aus`](#k-not-aus) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/killswitch/` | Kill switch with the scopes global, org, repo, service and service_repo: table, endpoints, check interface for router and Work API claim, stop to running runs and a page with a banner; lifting does not resume anything (FE-625). Not the pause of single runs (run state machine, 02). |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-1`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-1) | process | `-` | Acceptance of stage 1 without own product code: Gate A and Gate B runs, qualification row as reference qualification, leaderboard submission, project installation, shadow mode, decision on live, release and stage report. External effects (submission, tag, live) only with the owner. |
| [`pruef-proxy-operator-test`](#k-pruef-proxy-operator-test) | role | `apps/egress-proxy/src/llm-inspection/` | Module in the egress proxy of the worker host that, with profile operator_test, terminates TLS only for the LLM host, checks requests with the filter of the credential relay, books usage and passes the auth header on unchanged and never logged (ADR-18, FE-534). No credential replacement as with the relay and no path for other hosts (they go through as a tunnel). |
| [`reviewer-analyzer-ingest`](#k-reviewer-analyzer-ingest) | service | `services/reviewer/src/controller/analyzers/` | Fetches SARIF bytes from CI artifacts (optionally code scanning) with size limits into the BlobStore and feeds the normalized analyzer findings as a candidate signal into the finder context and the verifier (ADR-40); from stage 2 on also findings from analyzer run. Never parses in the controller (FE-821) and never produces unverified findings (FE-822). |
| [`reviewer-ausgabe`](#k-reviewer-ausgabe) | service | `services/reviewer/src/controller/post/` | Builds from verified rows in findings the write requests review, check and thread_resolve to the Effect Gateway, the summary, the check ai-review without silent green and the status row; in shadow mode the effects land in the eval log. The executors themselves belong to the Effect Gateway (1-E05-T08 to 1-E05-T11). |
| [`reviewer-befunde`](#k-reviewer-befunde) | service | `services/reviewer/src/findings/` | Turns verifier verdicts into findings: fingerprint v1, deterministic filter chain, noise filter, redaction and storage in findings together with ReviewArtifact and candidate blob. The tables findings and finding_feedback are created by 0-E02 (01 section 3.5); here repositories are created via the storage port and missing columns as an expand migration. |
| [`reviewer-bibliothek`](#k-reviewer-bibliothek) | service | `services/reviewer/src/library/` | The review pipeline once as the library reviewChange() with the port ReviewExecutor, so that PR review, the coder's self-review and local review compute the same fingerprints and filters. Never produces effects; output on GitHub is done only by the controller. |
| [`reviewer-finder`](#k-reviewer-finder) | service | `services/reviewer/src/jobs/find.handler.ts` | Runs per finder and shard a work item reviewer.find with AgentRuntime, read-only tools and schema output, and delivers candidates, never findings or effects (FE-801). Checking and filtering the candidates belongs to the verifier and the findings component. |
| [`reviewer-gate`](#k-reviewer-gate) | service | `services/reviewer/src/controller/gate-rules.ts` | Decides deterministically whether a reviewer run takes place (rules G1 to G9), and builds the PrepareOutput in the prepare job with the context tool and the gate model. The gate model never decides on skipping (FE-803). |
| [`reviewer-inkrement-und-feedback`](#k-reviewer-inkrement-und-feedback) | service | `services/reviewer/src/controller/increment/` | Carries findings across pushes (line mapping, recheck, addressed, outdated, withdrawn) and harvests feedback from the threads at run start and at merge into finding_feedback; from stage 6 on it verifies findings marked as fixed. No posting (that is done by reviewer-ausgabe). |
| [`reviewer-kontext-werkzeug`](#k-reviewer-kontext-werkzeug) | service | `services/reviewer/context-tool/` | Bundled Node script in the image sandbox-base that parses repo files and SARIF only in the sandbox and outputs exclusively schema JSON (FE-805). Never calls a model and has no network. |
| [`reviewer-kontextquellen`](#k-reviewer-kontextquellen) | service | `services/reviewer/src/controller/context-sources.ts` | Loads in the controller the context sources behind the port ContextSource (ticket and CI from stage 1, Learnings from 7a, knowledge base from 7) as sanitized untrusted parts with status. No tailoring to shards and no loading of other repos (FE-820). |
| [`reviewer-router-und-budget`](#k-reviewer-router-und-budget) | service | `services/reviewer/src/controller/router.ts` | Splits the run budget into prepare, finder, verifier and reserve, chooses depth and finders, distributes files to shards and builds the context package with a token budget per shard. Loads no context sources itself (that is done by reviewer-kontextquellen). |
| [`reviewer-suites`](#k-reviewer-suites) | eval | `services/reviewer/test/suites/` | Cases of the reviewer in the cross-cutting suites (injection, permissions, switched on alone, failure paths, installation and upgrade) and in the personal operator mode, as well as the permission tests against the real test app, from stage 6 on with approve. Does not provide the suite scaffold itself (that comes from 0-E22). |
| [`reviewer-verifier`](#k-reviewer-verifier) | service | `services/reviewer/src/jobs/verify.handler.ts` | Checks candidates deterministically for evidence (prefilter in the controller) and has them confirmed in the work item reviewer.verify in the modes read, recheck or build; sets the effective verifier mode before the claim (FE-835). May only lower severity (FE-810) and creates no findings in the DB. |
| [`service-reviewer`](#k-service-reviewer) | service | `services/reviewer/` | Scaffold of the reviewer: package with manifest, TypeBox schemas, configuration schema, controller as a single-service run with step plan, state per PR, inputs and commands as well as prompt loader and profile contribution. Not the domain steps (gate, finder, verifier, findings, output), which are separate components in the same package. |
| [`ui-run-record`](#k-ui-run-record) | ui | `apps/admin-ui/src/pages/RunRecord.tsx` | Read model RunRecordView from the tables of the control plane with redaction, endpoints for list, single view and export as well as the pages Runs and Run Record with deep link for status comments; writes nothing and does not compute the provenance marker itself (that is delivered by 2-E01-T12 from area 10). |

### Stage 2: Planner, Architect, Coder

Builds on stage 1.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`agent-ci`](#k-agent-ci) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/agent-ci/` | Enforces security.agent_ci: check of the CI variant on every claim of the coder (hook for QA and PR fixer) and in doctor with a cache by cacheKey, otherwise no_safe_ci; variant agent_fork with creation by the operator, push and PR from the fork and a real contract test. Not: the pure analysis of the workflow files (workflow-guard). |
| [`agent-step`](#k-agent-step) | package | `packages/agent-step/` | Shared run shell of every agent step of planner, architect and coder: builds the AgentTask with marked untrusted blocks, agent files from the base SHA and the mandatory output schema, reports foreign inputs before the start and holds the types of the step handler context. Not: single model calls (ModelProvider path), sandbox build, credentials or the permission check for foreign (herkunft-foreign-input). |
| [`analyzer-runner`](#k-analyzer-runner) | role | `apps/worker/src/analyzer-runner/` | Runs each analyzer in mode run in its own tool sandbox from its image (workspace read-only, rules from the base SHA, no network; from stage 10 on request only item_app or allowlist, 15 K9), compares with the baseline at the base SHA and maintains the offline databases. Not: the analyzer plugins themselves and not the gate decision (quality-gate). |
| [`arbeitsstand-snapshot`](#k-arbeitsstand-snapshot) | role | `apps/worker/src/work-snapshot/` | Saves the work state of an agent (workspace with .git and the configuration directory of the harness) after a secret scan as an archive and restores it for a clarifying question, steering, deadline expiry and rate limit pause; plus the deletion job after expiry. Not: a container image and not the environment snapshot (worker-umgebungs-snapshot). |
| [`blueprint`](#k-blueprint) | package | `packages/blueprint/` | Reads and checks the environment description of a repo (.agents/environment.yaml or the allowed devcontainer subset) at the base SHA and computes ResolvedEnvironment with snapshotKey from it. Not: building or starting a sandbox (worker-umgebungs-snapshot, worker-sandbox-phasen). |
| [`clarity`](#k-clarity) | package | `packages/clarity/` | Building block for the clarity gate of planner (stage 2) and triage (stage 7): builds the model request with schema and checks the response for clear, tooLarge, questions and split proposal. Not: the model call itself, which the step handler makes via the ModelProvider path. |
| [`coder-harte-gates`](#k-coder-harte-gates) | service | `services/coder/src/gates/` | The hard gates of the coder as one pure function, called by the worker (with repair) and the Effect Gateway (authoritative), and the approval G4 before the push for protected paths and deleted or skipped tests. Not: the self-check bundle (coder-self-check) and not the push itself (Effect Gateway). |
| [`coder-self-check`](#k-coder-self-check) | service | `services/coder/src/selfcheck/` | Deterministic checks in the worker in the role check after every agent round: tests against the base list, lint, build, format, repro for a bug fix, plan alignment as a hint, analyzers and platform gate; from stage 3 E2E smoke as a further check. Not: the hard gates (coder-harte-gates) and not the self-review with the reviewer (service-coder). |
| [`eval-saetze-stufe-2`](#k-eval-saetze-stufe-2) | eval | `eval/suites/p1-localization/` | Eval sets and adapters of stage 2 for Gate A and Gate B of Planner, Architect and Coder, plus the suite cases S1, S2, S4, S6 and hard gates of stage 2 (folders eval/suites/* and eval/adapters/* according to section 2.1). Not: the gate runs and reports (prozess-abnahme-stufe-2) and not the runner and statistics (eval-runner, eval-statistik). |
| [`herkunft-foreign-input`](#k-herkunft-foreign-input) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/provenance/` | Records in the control plane every untrusted input from a person that a service sees in the run, computes with a fresh permission query whether it is foreign, and sets runs.foreign_input_seen; QA and PR-Fixer report their inputs via the same service. Not: the block in the merge gate (stage 5) and no inputs without a person (code, CI logs, SARIF). |
| [`method-check`](#k-method-check) | package | `packages/method-check/` | Deterministic checkers for method artifacts: EARS patterns, required sections of the pinned MADR template, rule-based questions of the C4 review checklist and the call of the Mermaid check. Plus the pure building block of plan conformance (subpath @guildwork/method-check/conformance, FE-1077), which builds the model request and evaluates the response without calling a model itself. Not: model-based checks (Architect) and not the tool image mermaid-check (service-architect). |
| [`orchestrator-effekte`](#k-orchestrator-effekte) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/orchestrator-effects/` | Effects without a service that the orchestrator triggers itself, each with its own policy rule orchestrator.* and token profile: agent-approval-check, draft to ready, request reviewers from CODEOWNERS, link the ticket and set its status, status comment per run. Not: the executors of the effect types (effekt-executoren) and no exception from deny by default. |
| [`pipeline-ticket-to-pr`](#k-pipeline-ticket-to-pr) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/pipeline/` | Controls the pipeline ticket-to-pr in the control plane: stages with on_disabled and stage handlers per service, triggers by command and label, transitions up to awaiting_human_review, approval G1 manual and automatic including shadow measurement, shadow mode; later stages (QA, PR-Fixer, triage) dock on as stage handlers. Not: the work of the services themselves and not the deterministic effects (orchestrator-effekte). |
| [`plugin-analyzer-gitleaks`](#k-plugin-analyzer-gitleaks) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-gitleaks/` | Analyzer plugin for gitleaks with default rules plus own rules; its rule file is also used by the hard gate no_secret and the secret scan of the snapshots. Not: the execution of the gate (coder-harte-gates). |
| [`plugin-analyzer-opengrep`](#k-plugin-analyzer-opengrep) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-opengrep/` | Analyzer plugin for opengrep with its own default rule set and the repo rules from the base SHA, offline in the image. Not: the Opengrep rule collection or third-party registry rules (ADR-50). |
| [`plugin-analyzer-osv-scanner`](#k-plugin-analyzer-osv-scanner) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-osv-scanner/` | Analyzer plugin for osv-scanner with an offline database that the worker maintains (with air_gap from the registry mirror). Not: the osv cross-check of propose_dependency (propose-dependency). |
| [`plugin-analyzer-trivy`](#k-plugin-analyzer-trivy) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-trivy/` | Analyzer plugin for trivy (dependencies and IaC) with an offline database like osv-scanner. Not: container image scans of the releases (stage R). |
| [`propose-dependency`](#k-propose-dependency) | role | `apps/worker/src/dependency/` | Lets the coder request an additional dependency: check against the exact name allowlist in the control plane (MCP tool), clarifying question for a name that is not allowed, resolution of the transitive closure in the resolver container and osv check in the worker, storage in the registry cache. Not: filling from the lockfile (registry-cache) and no wildcards in the allowlist. |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-2`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-2) | process | `-` | Work without own product code for stage 2: reconciliation of the assumed names with the detailed designs 01 to 08, baseline values and data licenses, owner steps (eval credential, test organizations, architect shadow in the project installation), Gate A and Gate B runs, stage report and release with S8. Not: the eval sets and adapters themselves (eval-saetze-stufe-2). |
| [`quality-gate`](#k-quality-gate) | package | `packages/quality-gate/` | Decides from analyzer reports and metrics according to analysis.gate whether a head SHA passes the platform gate, and delivers the text of the check quality-gate; from stage 5 on, the merge gate reads the same decision. Not: running the analyzers (analyzer-runner) and not setting the check (coder via propose_check). |
| [`registry-cache`](#k-registry-cache) | package | `packages/registry-cache/` | Delivers packages from npm, PyPI and Go to the sandbox only from what the worker loaded from the lockfile in the setup phase, and never asks upstream; plus the worker parts apps/worker/src/registry. Not: loading single dependencies later at the agent's request (propose-dependency) and no other ecosystems in stage 2. |
| [`sarif`](#k-sarif) | package | `packages/sarif/` | Shared SARIF building blocks for analyzer runner, platform gate and reviewer: required field check, fingerprint, baseline comparison, properties bag for metrics. Not: running analyzers (analyzer-runner), not the analyzer contract v1alpha1 (contracts/vertrag-analyzer) and not the scaffold of the contract suite AN1 (contract-harness/an1-suite); both are created in the same task 2-E05-T01 but have their provider there. |
| [`service-architect`](#k-service-architect) | service | `services/architect/` | Reviews and creates architecture: design review on PRs with check ai-design-review, specification in EARS with C4 diagrams and tasks, ADR drafts according to MADR, threat model according to STRIDE and the mode conformance (building block in method-check, FE-1077); executes no repo code. Not: the method checkers (method-check) and not the integration into the pipeline (pipeline-ticket-to-pr). |
| [`service-coder`](#k-service-coder) | service | `services/coder/` | Implements an approved plan (or a ticket with --no-plan) in a sandbox with write and shell rights, checks itself, normalizes commits, builds bundle and PR text and reports push and draft PR as write requests; in addition clarifying question (L1), steering (L2) and agent-led environment setup (L4). Not: self-check bundle (coder-self-check), hard gates and G4 (coder-harte-gates), orchestrator effects such as agent-approval-check (orchestrator-effekte). |
| [`service-planner`](#k-service-planner) | service | `services/planner/` | Turns a ticket or a description into a checked, versioned plan (PlanArtifact) with an agent prompt per phase, read-only; publishes it as a plan comment and processes human edits. Not: the approval G1 and the shadow of G1 (pipeline-ticket-to-pr) and not the clarity gate itself (clarity). |
| [`worker-sandbox-phasen`](#k-worker-sandbox-phasen) | role | `apps/worker/src/phases/` | Takes every agent sandbox through setup, agent and check phase: secrets only in the setup phase, egress policy per item, service and phase with a probe before the harness start, connection log per item and sandbox without DNS resolver (in addition apps/worker/src/egress-policy and apps/worker/src/dns). Not: building the environment snapshot (worker-umgebungs-snapshot) and not the egress proxy itself (egress-proxy). |
| [`worker-umgebungs-snapshot`](#k-worker-umgebungs-snapshot) | role | `apps/worker/src/env-snapshot/` | Builds and reuses the environment snapshot per repo, snapshotKey and pool: post_build, baseline list of red tests, secret scan before storing. Not: phase switch (worker-sandbox-phasen) and not the work state of a run (arbeitsstand-snapshot). |
| [`workflow-guard`](#k-workflow-guard) | package | `packages/workflow-guard/` | Pure analysis of the workflow files of a repo at the base SHA and decision safe or no_safe_ci for agent_fork and guarded_workflows; anything unknown counts as unguarded. Not: reading at the provider, storing and the check per claim (agent-ci). |

### Stage 3: QA

Builds on stage 2.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`contracts-artefakte`](#k-contracts-artefakte) | package | `packages/contracts/src/artifacts/` | TypeBox schemas and types of the artifacts that QA, PR fixer and merge gate pass between stages and store in artifacts, including schema invariants and generated JSON Schemas; no flow logic and no storage. |

### Stage 7a: Learnings

Builds on stage 6.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`eval-suite-learnings`](#k-eval-suite-learnings) | eval | `eval/suites/learnings/` | Suite with the Learnings tests from 02 section 7 (secret redaction, expiry, scope auto, PR binding) plus approval delay and voting against real Postgres, and the measurement of citation validity across all output paths. Not here: S1 with injection via Learnings (cross-cutting suites) and the gates of the Reviewer (prozess-abnahme-stufe-7a). |
| [`learnings-lebenszyklus`](#k-learnings-lebenszyklus) | service | `services/indexer/src/learnings/` | Domain logic of the Learnings from sub-stage 7a: tables of the lifecycle, configuration knowledge.learnings, scope and PR binding, approval delay, voting and expiry, secret redaction and citation check, import and export including the CLI, and the admin API /admin/api/v1/learnings. Not here: storage and retrieval in the plugin (plugin-pg-kb), the creation of the tables learnings and learning_events in stage 6 (reviewer-chat-und-befehle) and the page of the admin UI (ui-learnings). |
| [`plugin-pg-kb`](#k-plugin-pg-kb) | plugin | `plugins/pg-kb/` | Default implementation of the KnowledgeStore contract on Postgres with pgvector: in 7a the capability LEARNINGS (store, vote, expiry, export, import, retrieval queryLearnings without vector search), from stage 7 writing the layers L1 to L3 via applyIncrement and rebuild (FE-1263) and the queries repoMap, symbolContext, impact, moduleSummary, search and learnings via vector search. Not here: the types of the contract (contracts), the life cycle as domain logic (learnings-lebenszyklus), the check of the deltas before writing (DeltaIntake in indexer-schichten) and the MCP tools kb.* (12). |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-7a`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-7a) | process | `-` | Qualification of the sub-stage 7a through the gates of the reviewer (Gate A with and without Learnings, Gate B reported), stage report with evidence per done criterion, release with S8 and upgrade test, follow-up list of the architecture. No own code. |
| [`service-indexer`](#k-service-indexer) | service | `services/indexer/` | Service indexer as a deterministic controller job in the control plane without sandbox and without model (FE-941): manifest, inputs via the router, layer state L0 with watermark and rebuild rules, L5 increment per merge (harvest, release PR binding, check citations at the default head). Not here: the layers L1 to L3, jobs with LayerDelta and Ask (stages 7, 12) and the domain logic of the Learnings (learnings-lebenszyklus). |
| [`ui-learnings`](#k-ui-learnings) | ui | `apps/admin-ui/src/pages/learnings/` | Page of the admin UI for Learnings: list with filters and metrics, approval view for pending_approval, actions approve, reject, confirm, invalidate by role and export button. Not here: the endpoints /admin/api/v1/learnings (learnings-lebenszyklus). |

### Stage 7: Knowledge base, standards, triage

Builds on stage 7a.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`embedder`](#k-embedder) | service | `services/embedder/` | Computes embeddings with a local model under a free license on CPU, only in the internal network of the control plane, own image with bundled model and checksum (FE-1205, O7). Not a service in the sense of the service manifests: no work items, no effects, no network to the outside; addressed only via the ModelProvider local-embed. |
| [`eval-saetze-stufe-7`](#k-eval-saetze-stufe-7) | eval | `eval/sets/` | The eval sets and adapters of stage 7 (sets under eval/sets/<id>/ according to 07 section 2.2, FE-1268; adapters under eval/adapters/kb-*, gh-aw-triage) with their reports: choice of the embedding model (K5), KB approval for the Reviewer (K1), Ask against reference agents (K4, K3), rules (ST1), triage (T1, T2 and comparison with gh-aw), plus the repo mode of T1 for the gate triage_t1. Not here: cross-cutting suites S1 to S8, stage report and release (prozess-abnahme-stufe-7), eval runner and statistics (area 07). |
| [`indexer-schichten`](#k-indexer-schichten) | service | `services/indexer/src/jobs/` | Extends the service indexer from 7a with the layers L1 (structure), L2 (summaries) and L3 (full text and vectors), the item index for issues and PRs, the embedding of the Learnings and the mode ask; plus the acceptance of the LayerDeltas in the control plane (apps/control-plane/src/kb/) with the watermark only after success. Not here: L0 and L5 including the Learnings lifecycle (7a), the query implementation in plugins/pg-kb and the tools kb.* of the platform MCP. |
| [`kb`](#k-kb) | package | `packages/kb/` | Shared types and pure functions of the knowledge base from stage 7: layers L0 to L5, the LayerDelta as the result of the indexer jobs, the query types of the KnowledgeStore, the hybrid search with RRF and the types of the kb.* tools. No database access and no query implementation (that lives in plugins/pg-kb), no jobs (service indexer). |
| [`kb-indexer`](#k-kb-indexer) | package | `packages/kb-indexer/` | Runs in the sandbox of the indexer jobs L1 and L3: parses repo files with web-tree-sitter, splits them into chunks and builds a LayerDelta from them, called via the command gw-kb-indexer. Never writes to the database and calls no model; planning, acceptance of the delta and embedding belong to the service indexer. |
| [`plugin-model-local-embed`](#k-plugin-model-local-embed) | plugin | `plugins/model-local-embed/` | Connects the service embedder as a ModelProvider with the capability EMBEDDINGS to the control plane; without a reachable service it reports EMBEDDINGS none, and the core switches off vector search per rule 2. No text model: generate answers unsupported, the resolver allows it only as knowledge.embed_model. |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-7`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-7) | process | `-` | Completes stage 7: owner steps for license requests (an account for the reference measurement with Codex CLI is dropped, O28), cross-cutting suites S1 (triage injection, KB, visibility), S2, S4 and S6 of the stage, stage report with Gate B status per service, qualification rows and signed release with S8 and upgrade from 7a. Builds no product function and no eval sets (eval-saetze-stufe-7). |
| [`service-standards`](#k-service-standards) | service | `services/standards/` | Measures per rule (rule_id) findings, acceptance and addressed rate, derives rule candidates from accepted feedback, proposes them as a PR on .agents/rules/, compiles confirmed model findings into ast-grep or Opengrep rules with test cases and proposes the withdrawal of weak rules. The only write request is propose_change on .agents/rules/; the service activates no rule itself (merge by CODEOWNERS, auto_activate only at installation level) and loads no guidelines (that is done by @guildwork/guidelines). |
| [`service-triage`](#k-service-triage) | service | `services/triage/` | Classifies new issues without a shell (duplicates and related items with visibility check, labels, assignees, repo, spam and slop, clarity), checks the result deterministically and publishes per property according to configuration; closing only with auto_close and a green T1 gate of the repo. In stage 7 only a single-service run; as the first stage of ticket-to-pr only from stage 9 (FE-1221). The GitHub methods (setLabels, linkItems, closeAsDuplicate) and the executors do not belong here. |

**Grows:** [`cli-doctor`](#k-cli-doctor), [`compose-buendel`](#k-compose-buendel), [`config-resolver`](#k-config-resolver), [`container-images`](#k-container-images), [`credential-broker`](#k-credential-broker), [`effekt-executoren`](#k-effekt-executoren), [`eval-dienst`](#k-eval-dienst), [`eval-querschnitts-suites`](#k-eval-querschnitts-suites), [`plattform-mcp`](#k-plattform-mcp), [`plugin-github-issues`](#k-plugin-github-issues), [`plugin-github-scm`](#k-plugin-github-scm), [`policy-engine`](#k-policy-engine), [`prozess-eval-konten-und-lizenzen`](#k-prozess-eval-konten-und-lizenzen), [`guidelines`](#k-guidelines), [`reviewer-kontextquellen`](#k-reviewer-kontextquellen), [`clarity`](#k-clarity), [`plugin-pg-kb`](#k-plugin-pg-kb)

### Stage 8: Jira, further providers and bases

Builds on stage 2, 0b.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`adf`](#k-adf) | package | `packages/adf/` | Pure functions without network and state that convert platform Markdown into Atlassian Document Format and read ADF from tickets and comments as Markdown (FE-1224, FE-1311). No Jira client, no sanitization of untrusted content and no permission check. |
| [`driver-blob-gcs`](#k-driver-blob-gcs) | driver | `drivers/blob-gcs/` | Driver of the BlobStore contract for Google Cloud Storage with signed URLs, versioning and retention per bucket setting, sign-in ambient or via the own issuer (FE-1340). No lifecycle management of the bucket; the bucket is created by the OpenTofu module gcp or by the operator. |
| [`driver-identity-aws`](#k-driver-identity-aws) | driver | `drivers/identity-aws/` | Driver of the CloudIdentity contract for AWS: assume the role of the items via STS (aws_sts, result as JSON per FE-1325), ambient or via web identity with the JWT of the own issuer (FE-1340). Creates no IAM roles (OpenTofu module aws or operator). |
| [`driver-identity-azure-managed-identity`](#k-driver-identity-azure-managed-identity) | driver | `drivers/identity-azure-managed-identity/` | Driver of the CloudIdentity contract for Azure: token of the managed identity (ambient) or Entra application with federated sign-in via the own issuer, exchange entra for Foundry and anthropic_wif (FE-1324, FE-1340). No creation of identities or roles. |
| [`driver-identity-gcp`](#k-driver-identity-gcp) | driver | `drivers/identity-gcp/` | Driver of the CloudIdentity contract for Google Cloud: identity token of the metadata service, exchange gcp_sts via Workload Identity Federation for the access token of the item service account and anthropic_wif, ambient or via the own issuer (FE-1340). Creates no service accounts. |
| [`driver-secret-aws-secretsmanager`](#k-driver-secret-aws-secretsmanager) | driver | `drivers/secret-aws-secretsmanager/` | Driver of the SecretStore contract for AWS Secrets Manager with get, put (WRITE) and optionally sign via KMS (SIGN only with a proven probe); one secret per name with JSON fields (FE-1341). Creates no KMS keys and no IAM permissions. |
| [`driver-secret-gcp-secretmanager`](#k-driver-secret-gcp-secretmanager) | driver | `drivers/secret-gcp-secretmanager/` | Driver of the SecretStore contract for Google Secret Manager with get, put as a new version (WRITE) and optionally sign via Cloud KMS (SIGN only with a proven probe); one secret per name with JSON fields (FE-1341). Creates no keys and no permissions. |
| [`helm-chart`](#k-helm-chart) | delivery | `deploy/helm/guildwork/` | Helm chart for operation on Kubernetes: separate deployments for web, orchestrator, worker pools and egress proxy from signed images by digest, migrate as a hook before the rollout, sandbox namespace with NetworkPolicy, values schema; plus the S8 run on kind and k3d (FE-1231). No database in the chart, no ingress; the ExecutionBackend k8s is the separate component plugin-exec-k8s. |
| [`identitaetsverknuepfung`](#k-identitaetsverknuepfung) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/identity/` | Links an account of a ticket system (Jira) with an SCM account (GitHub) only through OAuth confirmation of both sides by the user themselves, with the page Link accounts, revocation and audit (FE-1225, FE-1312, FE-1313). Not included: the permission AND check in the router, which only calls resolve, and the base model of the tables identities and identity_links (01). |
| [`plugin-backend-ci-dispatch-github`](#k-plugin-backend-ci-dispatch-github) | plugin | `plugins/backend-ci-dispatch-github/` | Starts work items as one-shot workers in GitHub Actions of a runner repo: plugin with dispatch and minting of the dispatch token, dispatcher job ci-dispatch-tick with the table dispatch_records in the control plane, template of the runner workflow, nested setup in the job, slot limit, expiry and metrics (ADR-45, FE-1350 to FE-1353). Not included: the OIDC login at the Work API (work-api), the mode --once (worker) and the broker profile dispatch (credential-broker). |
| [`plugin-codex`](#k-plugin-codex) | plugin | `plugins/codex/` | Second harness: adapter for Codex CLI (codex exec --json --output-schema) as AgentRuntime with install via PinnedVersion, event mapping, credential kind openai via the relay and chatgpt as an operator mode (FE-1229, FE-1330 to FE-1332). Not included: the resolver rule checkCodexCredentials (provider config-resolver-regeln/codex-credentials, built in the same task), the CLI itself (loaded at the operator, never into the image), the relay extension by upstreamKind openai and the price calculation (FE-1360). |
| [`plugin-exec-k8s`](#k-plugin-exec-k8s) | plugin | `plugins/exec-k8s/` | ExecutionBackend k8s, loaded in the worker pod: sandbox per item as a pod with RuntimeClass in the sandbox namespace, NetworkPolicy per item only to the egress proxy, binding at the proxy via the pod IP (FE-1345, FE-1346). No Docker in the pod, no access to secrets; the Helm chart creates the namespace and the RBAC. |
| [`plugin-jira-cloud`](#k-plugin-jira-cloud) | plugin | `plugins/jira-cloud/` | One plugin with the kinds TriggerSource (ingress via admin webhook or automation relay, catch-up via JQL) and WorkItemProvider (read tickets and write them via the Effect Gateway) for Jira Cloud (ADR-09). Not included: identity linking, permission AND check and visibility of ticket targets (control plane) and ADF conversion (@guildwork/adf). |
| [`plugin-model-bedrock`](#k-plugin-model-bedrock) | plugin | `plugins/model-bedrock/` | ModelProvider for single calls via Amazon Bedrock (Vercel AI SDK), executed in the worker as work item model_call, access via the grant bedrock and the relay with SigV4 or in passthrough (FE-1327). Not included: the start path bedrock of the harness claude-code, the STS identity (driver-identity-aws) and the relay extension. |
| [`plugin-model-foundry`](#k-plugin-model-foundry) | plugin | `plugins/model-foundry/` | ModelProvider for single calls to Anthropic models in Microsoft Foundry (Vercel AI SDK), executed in the worker as work item model_call, access via the grant foundry (FE-1327). Not included: the start path foundry of the harness claude-code and the identity (driver-identity-azure-managed-identity); never for eu repos (FE-1326). |
| [`plugin-model-vertex`](#k-plugin-model-vertex) | plugin | `plugins/model-vertex/` | ModelProvider for single calls to Anthropic models on Vertex AI (Vercel AI SDK), executed in the worker as work item model_call, access via the grant vertex (FE-1327). Not included: the start path vertex of the harness claude-code and the identity (driver-identity-gcp); EU applies only after evidence (FE-1326). |
| [`pricing`](#k-pricing) | package | `packages/pricing/` | Versioned price tables per provider with source and retrieval date, loader into price_entries (role migrate only) with operator overrides, and lookup for reservation, billing and eval reports (FE-1230, FE-1255, FE-1360 to FE-1362). Never loads from the network at runtime; plugins and workers do not import the package. |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-8`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-8) | process | `-` | Work without own product code: fixtures and cassettes from the public documentation for Jira and the cloud providers (O28, 13 FE-1366), runner repo and dispatch app on the owner's GitHub account, apply workflows; Jira test site, cloud accounts, real OpenTofu applies and qualification runs per combination only as optional owner runs; suites, stage report and signed release of stage 8. Builds no plugins or drivers; costs money only with the owner's go (O22). |
| [`tofu-cloud-module`](#k-tofu-cloud-module) | delivery | `deploy/tofu/` | OpenTofu modules for the bases aws, gcp and hetzner as well as the module host-prepare, which renders host-prepare.sh as a cloud-init part (FE-1232), with a check that no secret is a variable or output. Not included: the modules generic-vm and azure (stage 0b) and real applies (owner, prozess-abnahme-stufe-8). |
