### Stage 9: Breadth and hardening

Builds on stage 7, 8.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`beispiele-dritte`](#k-beispiele-dritte) | delivery | `examples/` | Templates for third parties that build only against the published schemas and plugin.proto and run as third_party via the subprocess host; proof that the contracts suffice without internal packages. Not: production plugins, import of @guildwork packages (FE-1433). |
| [`coder-erweiterte-steuerung`](#k-coder-erweiterte-steuerung) | service | `services/coder/src/children/` | Extended steering of the coder: handoff to a human and resumption (services/coder/src/handoff.ts), child steps over disjoint phases with a deterministic integrator (services/coder/src/children/) and best-of-N with deterministic selection (services/coder/src/best-of-n.ts). Not: new run states for children, stacked PRs, combination of child runs and best-of-N (FE-1438). |
| [`plugin-analyzer-ast-grep`](#k-plugin-analyzer-ast-grep) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-ast-grep/` | Runs the ast-grep rules compiled by standards under .agents/rules/ast-grep/ from the base SHA in the review, offline, with the same engine version as the image engines. Not: its own default rule set, third-party rule collections or the compiling and testing of rules (that is done by standards). |
| [`plugin-azure-devops`](#k-plugin-azure-devops) | plugin | `plugins/azure-devops/` | Azure DevOps as a code hoster with service hook ingress (weak), SCMProvider for repos and pull requests and WorkItemProvider for work items. Not: HMAC signature (does not exist), merge (FE-1446). |
| [`plugin-backend-microvm`](#k-plugin-backend-microvm) | plugin | `plugins/backend-microvm/` | ExecutionBackend with isolation microvm via Kata as a Docker runtime, reported only after a probe, plus the evidence that repo code of the class external_code never falls back to weaker isolation, and the block until the pen test. Not: an own copy of the Docker code (FE-1421), fallback to gVisor (FE-1424). |
| [`plugin-bitbucket`](#k-plugin-bitbucket) | plugin | `plugins/bitbucket/` | Bitbucket Cloud as a code hoster with HMAC webhook, SCMProvider with single inline comments, Code Insights for status and annotations, and labels as comment markers. Not: WorkItemProvider (01 matrix 11.1 dropped), merge. |
| [`plugin-gemini-cli`](#k-plugin-gemini-cli) | plugin | `plugins/gemini-cli/` | AgentRuntime for Gemini CLI only with api_key via the relay or vertex via CloudIdentity, with turn limit and abort. Not: login via a personal account in platform code (FE-1419). |
| [`plugin-gitea`](#k-plugin-gitea) | plugin | `plugins/gitea/` | One plugin for Gitea and Forgejo with flavor (FE-1401): HMAC webhook, batch review, commit status plus summary, issues; tests against both as containers in CI. Not: separate packages per fork, merge. |
| [`plugin-gitlab`](#k-plugin-gitlab) | plugin | `plugins/gitlab/` | GitLab as the second code hoster with TriggerSource, SCMProvider and WorkItemProvider (issues) in the control plane, review output via the fallback chain and the weak token tier in the broker. ### Stage 10: Edge layers

Builds on stage 3, 4.

**New:**

| Component | Kind | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`eval-saetze-docs`](#k-eval-saetze-docs) | eval | `eval/sets/do1/` | Eval sets, gate file and adapter for the docs service: DO1 (drift, gate A), DO3 (docstrings), DO4 (release notes), DO2 as a report part only after license clarification; stored per 07 under eval/sets/<id>/ (FE-1537). Not for F4 and CD1 of the PR fixer. |
| [`kampagnen`](#k-kampagnen) | role | `apps/control-plane/src/campaigns/` | One change by recipe across many repos: parent run with plan and G1, per repo a normal pipeline run campaign-child with all gates, a shared budget in the ledger key campaign, abort on failure rate, admin API and admin UI. No auto-merge, no Coder child runs from stage 9 (FE-1236) and no replacement for the limits of the repos. |
| [`plugin-analyzer-axe`](#k-plugin-analyzer-axe) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-axe/` | Checks the accessibility of the app started in the QA E2E item with axe-core and returns SARIF with a pseudo path per route; plus the QA step e2e_a11y. Never blocks in stage 10: findings are hints, the QA verdict stays unchanged (FE-1526). |
| [`plugin-analyzer-git-cliff`](#k-plugin-analyzer-git-cliff) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-git-cliff/` | Returns version, tag, date, commits and breaking list deterministically from Conventional Commits as a properties bag for the mode release of the docs service. Produces no findings and no prose; version and date never come from a model. |
| [`plugin-analyzer-infracost`](#k-plugin-analyzer-infracost) | plugin | `plugins/analyzer-infracost/` | Produces a cost diff for IaC (HCL) between base and head as a properties bag that the Reviewer shows deterministically in its summary. No findings, no prompt context; whether price data needs an account is unverified (backlog M35, until then byo_license). |
| [`plugin-incident-handoff`](#k-plugin-incident-handoff) | plugin | `plugins/incident-handoff/` | TriggerSource for handoffs from monitoring and incident tools via Standard Webhooks signature; in addition the handoff in the control plane (incident/intake), which creates at most one ticket or, via a route with a responsible person, a fix job. No dedicated SRE agent (ADR-49); the sender never gets write permission. |
| [`plugin-sentry`](#k-plugin-sentry) | plugin | `plugins/sentry/` | TriggerSource for Seer events from Sentry, mapped to the same event and the same body as incident-handoff; signature headers and fields are unverified and are verified in 10-E03-T02 against documentation and recording. No handoff logic of its own (it lives in incident/intake). |
| [`prfixer-modi`](#k-prfixer-modi) | service | `services/prfixer/src/modes/` | Two modes of the PR fixer as strategies of the same controller: dependency_update repairs red bot update PRs as a stacked PR, manifest and lockfile only via the package manager; ci_doctor finds the cause of red CI on the default branch and keeps updating the same issue. Not for the PR fixer core (11 section 2.4), not for pushes or reruns on the default branch and not for the executor issue (effect catalog). |
| [`prozess-abnahme-stufe-10`](#k-prozess-abnahme-stufe-10) | process | `-` | Owner steps and acceptance of stage 10: license request for CodeWikiBench and DocAgent, legal assessment of Renovate, stage report with evidence per done criterion, S8 with upgrade and signed release. No product code; no agent gives legal advice, it only prepares drafts and decision sheets. |
| [`service-docs`](#k-service-docs) | service | `services/docs/` | Keeps documentation current without changing code: drift check on PRs (never blocking), docstrings of touched symbols as a follow-up PR, docs PR after merge and release notes as a changelog PR. Not for merges, tags or publications (always done by a human) and not for code changes. |

## Part 2: Component sheets

### K `ci-workflows`

**CI workflow set with ci-ok as the only required check, Renovate configuration, CI measurement** (tool, from stage R). The workflow set of the product repo: ci.yml with the job split ts, tools, security and ci-ok as the only required check, CodeQL, Scorecard, daily full scans of main (vulnerabilities and ScanCode), Renovate configuration and the measurement of waiting time and concurrency. Not the release, portability and acceptance workflows of later stages and not the deny jobs (denylist-scanner).

- Path: `.github/workflows/`
- Design: [00-codebase-and-conventions.md#211-ci-workflows](00-codebase-and-conventions.md#211-ci-workflows), [00-codebase-and-conventions.md#42-ci-run-and-ci-ok](00-codebase-and-conventions.md#42-ci-run-and-ci-ok), [00-codebase-and-conventions.md#210-check-tools](00-codebase-and-conventions.md#210-check-tools)
- Built by: R-E03-T01, R-E03-T02, R-E03-T03, R-E03-T04, R-E05-T04, R-E05-T10

### K `core`

**Package core: Result, errors, IDs, time, hash, secrets, logging, telemetry facade, redaction** (package, from stage R). Base types for every package: result and error types with problem+json, IDs and canonical JSON, clock and randomness, SecretValue, logger with redaction, metric and trace facade with catalog and the single source of redaction rules. Without workspace dependencies and without the OTel SDK (telemetry starts that).

### K `denylist-scanner`

### K `lizenz-gate`

**License gate: SPDX headers, allowlist, ScanCode, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, toolchain.md** (tool, from stage R). Not the license gate of the images (release-werkzeuge, 0-E21).

### K `opengrep-regeln`

**Opengrep rules of the repo with rule tests (write subpath and write methods only in executors, environment, clock, foreign content)** (tool, from stage R). Own Opengrep rules under Apache-2.0 with rule tests that enforce code rules within packages (write subpath of the plugins only in the executors of the Effect Gateway, no model credentials from the environment, process.env only in loader modules, no direct clock, no foreign content in the log). From 0-E09-T05 additionally the rule single write path for calls of write methods (00 FE-054, 04 FE-445; the type-aware test from 04 FE-439 is dropped). Not the analyzer plugin for customer repos (plugin-analyzer-opengrep).

- Path: `.opengrep/`
- Design: [00-codebase-and-conventions.md#210-check-tools](00-codebase-and-conventions.md#210-check-tools), [00-codebase-and-conventions.md#6-security](00-codebase-and-conventions.md#6-security), [04-effects-audit-credentials.md#6-security](04-effects-audit-credentials.md#6-security)
- Built by: R-E02-T04, 0-E09-T05

### K `schichtenpruefung`

**Layer check of the package dependencies and package generator** (tool, from stage R). Enforces the allowed dependencies between workspace packages from quality/layers.toml (package.json, imports, testkit only in tests, freedom from cycles) and creates new packages only via the generator. Checks no rules within a package (Opengrep does that) and no external licenses (license gate).

### K `alarm-automat`

**Alert state machine with rules, sinks and health sources** (role, from stage 0). Computes the required alerts itself in the role orchestrator from stored facts, keeps their state in the table alerts, delivers them via log, webhook and later notifier and shows them in the admin API. No third-party alarm backend; rules of other areas dock on via the rule list.

Not here: tables, triggers and the functions audit_head and audit_insert (migration in area 01) and the redaction rules (core).

### K `config-installation`

**Configuration loader of the installation with published schema** (package, from stage 0). Reads installation.yaml once at the start of every role, checks it strictly (YAML 1.2, unknown keys, driver keys, cross-checks), freezes it and publishes the schema and the reference of the default values. Never resolves secrets and is not the resolver of the org, repo group and repo layers (config-resolver).

**Config resolver: schemas installation, org, repo, loading at the base SHA, merge, fail closed, snapshot, repo_overrides** (package, from stage 0). Provides the effective configuration of a run: schemas with x-merge and x-qualification, loading of the org, group and repo files at the pinned SHA, merging only in the stricter direction, fail closed, consistency rules, snapshot with qualification_key per service, expression language and repo_overrides. Not here: the loader of installation.yaml (config-installation), the profile and key themselves (qualifikationsprofil) and the resolver rules of the plugin areas (config-resolver-regeln).

- Path: `packages/config/`, package `@guildwork/config`

### K `config-resolver-regeln`

**Resolver rules: harness pins, reachability, personal operator mode, plan critique, agent_fork, merge mode, relay proof, codex, data path** (package, from stage 0). Pure check rules that the config resolver calls when loading the effective configuration and the orchestrator calls at claim time; each rule rejects only the affected runtime, the service or the run, never the installation. The resolver itself, the hierarchy and the JSON Schema are built by config-resolver and config-installation; this component provides the rules and their schema additions.

- Path: `packages/config/src/rules/`, package `@guildwork/config`

### K `contracts`

**Package contracts: base types, contracts v1alpha1, driver contracts, sketches, plugin and service manifest, Analyzer and WorkItemProvider contract** (package, from stage 0). The only source of the types and schemas through which core, plugins, drivers and services talk to each other: base types, the eight binding contracts v1alpha1, sketches, plugin and service manifest with validation and later the binding contracts Analyzer and WorkItemProvider. Contains no network or database access; loader and transport are in plugin-rahmen, the event schema in event-schema, the harness in testkit.

### K `control-plane`

**Control plane program: role selection, roles web and orchestrator, health** (program, from stage 0). One program for all roles of the control plane: selects the roles from the argument, starts HTTP (web) and pg-boss workers (orchestrator), mounts the areas via WebMount and reports readiness. Contains no domain logic itself; ingress, router, orchestrator, policy and ledger are separate components, the role ops belongs to detailed design 06.

- Path: `apps/control-plane/`, package `@guildwork/control-plane`
- Design: [02-control-plane.md#24-roles-and-processes](02-control-plane.md#24-roles-and-processes), [02-control-plane.md#41-ingress](02-control-plane.md#41-ingress), [02-control-plane.md#7-configuration](02-control-plane.md#7-configuration)
- Built by: 0-E02-T02, 0-E05-T10, 0-E18-T12, 8-E06-T01

### K `control-plane-ingress`

**Ingress with signature check, inbox, dedupe, reconcile and poll** (role, from stage 0). Accepts webhooks, relays and ci_event per plugin instance, checks the signature on the raw body before any parsing, puts raw data into the BlobStore and the inbox, normalizes asynchronously into events with dedupe and catches up via reconcile and poll. Decides nothing about routes, permissions or runs; the router does that.

### K `control-plane-orchestrator`

**Orchestrator with run state machine, intake, steps, deadlines, status comment, queues** (role, from stage 0). Drives every run according to the run state machine (one JSON file as the only source): intake with object lock and reservation, transitions in one transaction, steps via the service controllers, control commands, deadlines, status comment, lifting on upgrade, plus the list and registration of all queues. Decides no policy and no budget itself and never writes past the Effect Gateway.

### K `control-plane-router`

**Router: filter stages, repo assignment, route selection, permission check G0** (role, from stage 0). Assigns every new event to a route: cheap filters, repo assignment, fresh re-read against TOCTOU, configuration at the base SHA, route selection with deny by default and permission check G0 at the provider; the result is a RouteDecision or a skipped event. Creates no run and knows no object lock (FE-210); later stages only add routes, arguments and permission forms here.

### K `credential-broker`

**Credential broker: secrets, OIDC issuer, item token, SCM tokens, LLM grants, pool keys, profiles** (role, from stage 0). Issues short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials: secrets from the SecretStore with audit, SCM tokens per effect or per clone with exactly one repo and profile, item tokens, LLM grants per item and pool keys; publishes the JWKS of its own issuer. Never stores a token and never sees a subscription token; the key ring itself lives in the driver identity-self-issuer.

### K `credential-relay`

**Credential relay in the egress proxy (API key, WIF, SigV4)** (role, from stage 0). Holds the LLM credential of an item only in the memory of the egress proxy (Z1), accepts from the sandbox only model calls with the placeholder, checks them against the rules R1 to R10, sets the real header or the SigV4 signature and counts the usage. Does not book into the ledger itself and does not apply to the start path subscription.

- Path: `apps/egress-proxy/src/relay/`, package `@guildwork/egress-proxy`

### K `db`

**Package db: connection, tenant context with RLS, Kysely types, repositories** (package, from stage 0). Sole access of the control plane and the eval service to Postgres: connection per role, tenant context with row-level security, installation scope with a fixed list of callers, Kysely types, thin repositories and the maintenance jobs for partitions and retention. ### K `db-migrator`

**Migrator with gates, schema check at start and role migrate** (package, from stage 0). Applies the numbered SQL migrations forward only (lock against parallel runs, checksums, backup gate, halt points, minimum versions of PostgreSQL and pgvector) and checks at the start of each role whether schema and release match. Not here: content of the migrations (db-schema-kern and the areas), linter (migration-lint), flow of guildwork upgrade (CLI).

### K `db-queue`

**pg-boss foundation: start in the schema pgboss, sending within the transaction** (package, from stage 0). Encapsulates pg-boss behind QueueRuntime and sendInTx, so that jobs are created in the same transaction as their DB change and the unverified option names stay in one place. Knows no queue names and no handlers; the list of queues and the registration live in the orchestrator.

### K `db-schema-kern`

**Migrations 0001 to 0008 of the core tables with row-level security** (package, from stage 0). SQL migrations 0001 to 0008 with the core tables of stage 0 (DDL, constraints, indexes, partitioning, append-only protection of the audit) and tenant separation via row-level security. Not here: tables of individual areas and later stages (table directory, each its own migration of the building task), maintenance functions 0009 (db), domain logic of the writers.

### K `effect-gateway`

**Effect gateway: effect catalog, acceptance, idempotency, outbox, record and shadow, path and diff policies** (role, from stage 0). Sole write path to the outside: accepts write requests and platform effects, checks schema, target, policy, content and the checkers of later stages, assigns the idempotency key, keeps the outbox in effects and dispatches via the executors with retry and reconciliation. Calls no write method of a plugin itself (only the executors do that) and decides no policy rule POL-* (the policy engine does that).

### K `effekt-executoren`

**Executors per effect type** (role, from stage 0). Exactly one executor per effect type, which calls the write method of the plugin with the token per effect, sets the marker, reconciles after a crash and selects the fallback level; only here may write methods of the plugins be called. Not here: acceptance, policy, retry and ordering (effect gateway) and the plugin methods themselves (plugins).

### K `egress-proxy`

**Egress proxy: CONNECT with allowlist per item, control API, air gap, policy per phase** (program, from stage 0). Sole way of a sandbox to the outside: CONNECT only to exactly allowed hosts per item, binding to the item via the network interface, DNS only in the proxy, air gap as intersection, connection log per item; controlled by the worker via a control API. No TLS interception except in the inspection proxy, no database connection.

- Path: `apps/egress-proxy/`, package `@guildwork/egress-proxy`

### K `eval-adapter-harbor`

**Adapter Harbor with locked protocol** (eval, from stage 0). Maps tasks in the Harbor format to a ticket fixture with image by digest, fetches the patch from the eval log and checks it in the locked protocol in a fresh sandbox with the task's verifier. ### K `eval-core`

**Package eval-core: types and schemas for set, case, labels, reference qualification** (eval, from stage 0). Pure types, TypeBox schemas and contracts of the eval package without IO (set and case format, label and reference lines, adapter and scorer contract, reference values, eval report, reference qualification), shared by runner, control plane and all sets. Not for statistics, gates and judges (separate components in the same package) and not for run control or database access.

### K `eval-richter`

### K `eval-saetze-reviewer`

**Sets R1, R2, R4, R5 with scorers, labels and reference values** (eval, from stage 0). The eval sets of the reviewer as declarative pins with checksums (R2, R4, R5), own references and human labels (R1), the scorers per set, the judge prompt review-match and the read-off reference values; stage 0 builds pins, the scorers martian, reviewbench, swe-prbench, aacr, label schema and the first labeling round, stage 1 the scorer own-review, the calibration and the first real runs. Not for adapters, statistics or gate files and never for copies of third-party data (FE-728).

### K `limit-ledger`

**Limit ledger: buckets, reservation, consumption, settlement, time windows** (role, from stage 0). Hard limit for costs, runs, tokens and parallelism: key chain and buckets from the snapshot, atomic reservation across all keys before the run, booking of cumulative usage during the run with abort, settlement and release afterwards. Does not start or end runs itself; it reports budget_exhausted to the orchestrator.

### K `plugin-claude-code`

**AgentRuntime claude-code: manifest, run, event stream, contract suite, resume and steer** (plugin, from stage 0). AgentRuntime for the unmodified Claude Code CLI in the worker: installs the pinned harness with checksum into the sandbox, starts it via the hardened start path, translates the NDJSON stream into RuntimeEvents without plaintext and delivers AgentRunResult with usage, cost and limits; from stage 2 resume and steer. ### K `plugin-exec-docker`

**ExecutionBackend docker-sysbox and docker-gvisor** (plugin, from stage 0). ### K `plugin-github-scm`

**GitHub SCMProvider: read, write, push, merge, rerun, approve, check actions, SARIF** (plugin, from stage 0). Maps the SCMProvider contract to the GitHub API: read methods for control plane, platform MCP and services, write methods only for the Effect Gateway with a token per effect, push via Git bundle without force, and the optional methods of the later stages. Decides nothing itself: policy, push check and retry lie with the caller; plugin-github mints the token.

### K `plugin-model-claude-cli`

**ModelProvider claude-cli** (plugin, from stage 0). ### K `plugin-rahmen`

**Plugin framework: registry, loader, load conditions, capability resolver, retry, in-process transport** (package, from stage 0). Loads built-in plugin and driver packages per instance with the load conditions 1 to 15, runs the state machine of the instance, decides on capabilities and fallback levels, retries calls at the caller and wraps every plugin with time limit, error encapsulation and write protection. Persists nothing itself (the control plane writes plugin_instances) and starts no subprocess plugins in stage 0 (FE-536).

### K `policy-engine`

**Policy engine: deny by default, command covers effect, service mode, rules per service** (role, from stage 0). Pure function over stored facts that decides run start, service mode, write requests, platform effects and work items with rule IDs POL-nnn and logs every decision in policy_decisions. Never reads model text and executes nothing; the Effect Gateway executes effects, and the citation check itself lives there.

### K `socket-proxy`

**Socket proxy with allowlist and body check** (role, from stage 0). Sole holder of the Docker daemon socket on single-host: passes through to the worker only the Docker API calls that a sandbox needs, and checks on creation runtime, image digest, network, mounts, rights and label. Replaces no kernel boundary and knows no work items.

- Path: `apps/worker/src/socket-proxy/`, package `@guildwork/worker`

### K `telemetry`

**Package telemetry: OTel SDK start per role and instruments from the catalog** (package, from stage 0). Starts the OTel SDK in each role before other code, registers the metrics of the catalog with cardinality protection, gives the harness the OTel environment and delivers the collector as a Compose fragment. Only apps use it; packages measure via the facade in core. Not the product telemetry (produkt-telemetrie).

### K `testkit`

**Package testkit: Postgres container, fixtures, clock, logs, secret scan, fakes** (package, from stage 0). Shared test helpers of all areas: real Postgres per test file, controllable clock and randomness, log capture, secret check, HTTP replay with network block and the fakes and check helpers that tests of several areas need. Only in test files; contract harness and E2E stack in the same package are separate components. Building blocks whose signature another area defines (test IdP, fake Anthropic, telemetry sink, Azure recorder from 06 section 2.17, expectRecordedEffects from 04 section 2.1.6) are built by testkit as well, but they are offered there (00 FE-060).

### K `work-api`

**Work API: work items, claim, lease, drain, results and artifact upload** (role, from stage 0). The only way work gets from the control plane to workers and results come back: create and revoke work items, claim with capability matching, leases with heartbeat, results, artifact upload and drain. Does not decide on run states (orchestrator), budgets (ledger) or write requests (Effect Gateway).

### K `work-item-umschlag`

**Work item envelope, result, grants and write request schemas** (package, from stage 0). Versioned TypeBox schemas including types for everything that travels between control plane and worker: envelope, grants, result, error and Work API messages. The write request schemas (ProposalV1) are offered by the Effect Gateway (FE-345). No logic, no storage location and no check of rights; the envelope never carries a secret.

### K `worker`

**Worker binary: configuration, claim loop, checked capabilities, item lifecycle** (program, from stage 0). Program guildwork-worker on the worker host (Z1): fetches work items only outbound via the Work API, checks its capabilities itself, clones in Z1, runs each item in a fresh sandbox and always destroys it. Holds no database connection, calls no model itself and decides no write requests.

### K `worker-harness-umgebung`

**Harness environment from allowlist and start path subscription in the worker** (role, from stage 0). Builds in the worker the environment of the harness process from an empty environment and an allowlist per credential kind, reads the subscription token per item from the host file of the operator and gives the runtime the harness cache directory of the worker host (copied in via copyIn, FE-333). Does not start the harness itself (that is done by the runtime plugin via the item lifecycle) and stores no credential.

### K `pruef-proxy-operator-test`

**Inspection proxy for the LLM endpoint (profile operator_test)** (role, from stage 1). Module in the egress proxy of the worker host that, with profile operator_test, terminates TLS only for the LLM host, checks requests with the filter of the credential relay, books usage and passes the auth header on unchanged and never logged (ADR-18, FE-534). ### K `reviewer-verifier`

**Evidence check, verifier read, recheck and build** (service, from stage 1). Checks candidates deterministically for evidence (prefilter in the controller) and has them confirmed in the work item reviewer.verify in the modes read, recheck or build; sets the effective verifier mode before the claim (FE-835). ### K `pipeline-ticket-to-pr`

**PipelineRunner ticket-to-pr with stages, triggers, transitions, G1 and shadow** (role, from stage 2). Controls the pipeline ticket-to-pr in the control plane: stages with on_disabled and stage handlers per service, triggers by command and label, transitions up to awaiting_human_review, approval G1 manual and automatic including shadow measurement, shadow mode; later stages (QA, PR-Fixer, triage) dock on as stage handlers. Not: the work of the services themselves and not the deterministic effects (orchestrator-effekte).

### K `service-coder`

**Coder: agent phases, self-review, commits and bundle, draft PR, L1, L2, L4** (service, from stage 2). Implements an approved plan (or a ticket with --no-plan) in a sandbox with write and shell rights, checks itself, normalizes commits, builds bundle and PR text and reports push and draft PR as write requests; in addition clarifying question (L1), steering (L2) and agent-led environment setup (L4). Not: self-check bundle (coder-self-check), hard gates and G4 (coder-harte-gates), orchestrator effects such as agent-approval-check (orchestrator-effekte).

### K `service-planner`

**Planner: research, consistency, synthesis, plan verifier, critique, PlanArtifact** (service, from stage 2). Turns a ticket or a description into a checked, versioned plan (PlanArtifact) with an agent prompt per phase, read-only; publishes it as a plan comment and processes human edits. Not: the approval G1 and the shadow of G1 (pipeline-ticket-to-pr) and not the clarity gate itself (clarity).

- Path: `services/planner/`, package `@guildwork/service-planner`
- Design: [10-planner-architect-coder.md#210-planner-servicesplanner](10-planner-architect-coder.md#210-planner-servicesplanner), [10-planner-architect-coder.md#41-planner-run](10-planner-architect-coder.md#41-planner-run), [10-planner-architect-coder.md#82-planner-and-clarity-gate-2-e02](10-planner-architect-coder.md#82-planner-and-clarity-gate-2-e02)

### K `merge-ausfuehrung-und-nachlauf`

**Merge with fencing, states merge_gate and merging, post-merge watch, revert and fallback to human with UI page repo_overrides** (role, from stage 5). Executes a decision merge: fresh reading of hold, stop and request changes, agent-approval-check and effect merge with fencing via decisionId, states merge_gate and merging in the run state machine, post-merge watch at the merge SHA with a deterministic revert step and fallback to human via repo_overrides including the admin UI; does not evaluate conditions and does not build the executor merge.

### K `merge-gate`

**Merge gate: facts, conditions C00 to C13, waiting window** (role, from stage 5). Deterministic merge gate in the orchestrator: load facts fresh (fail closed), conditions C00 to C13 as a pure function, every evaluation as a row in merge_gate_decisions, waiting window with deadline and evidence of the branch protection; no service, no model and no merge call (that is done by merge-ausfuehrung-und-nachlauf).

### K `auto-approve`

**Automatic approval of human PRs with withdrawal** (service, from stage 6). Detects agent PRs, decides deterministically after a full run on the approval of a human PR (conditions from ADR-61, no model), stores the decision, triggers the platform effects approve_human and withdraw_approve and shows why auto_approve has no effect. Not here: the executors approve_human and withdraw_approve (04), the SCM methods approve, withdrawApprove, approvalProtection (GitHub plugin) and the contract tests against GitHub.

### K `reviewer-chat-und-befehle`

**Chat in the thread, remember, pause and resume** (service, from stage 6). Replies in threads of the platform (classification, finding feedback with actor_role, reply via propose_reply) and the commands @agent remember, @agent pause and @agent review including the pause state (services/reviewer/src/chat/ and src/pause/); in stage 6 creates the tables learnings and learning_events and stores candidates. Not here: the lifecycle of the Learnings from 7a on (learnings-lebenszyklus) and the gate that reads the pause (08).

### K `plugin-pg-kb`

**KnowledgeStore pg-kb: learnings, queries L1 to L3, vector search** (plugin, from stage 7a). Default implementation of the KnowledgeStore contract on Postgres with pgvector: in 7a the capability LEARNINGS (store, vote, expiry, export, import, retrieval queryLearnings without vector search), from stage 7 writing the layers L1 to L3 via applyIncrement and rebuild (FE-1263) and the queries repoMap, symbolContext, impact, moduleSummary, search and learnings via vector search. Not here: the types of the contract (contracts), the life cycle as domain logic (learnings-lebenszyklus), the check of the deltas before writing (DeltaIntake in indexer-schichten) and the MCP tools kb.* (12).

### K `indexer-schichten`

**Indexer L1 to L3, increment with watermark, item index, Ask flow** (service, from stage 7). Extends the service indexer from 7a with the layers L1 (structure), L2 (summaries) and L3 (full text and vectors), the item index for issues and PRs, the embedding of the Learnings and the mode ask; plus the acceptance of the LayerDeltas in the control plane (apps/control-plane/src/kb/) with the watermark only after success. Not here: L0 and L5 including the Learnings lifecycle (7a), the query implementation in plugins/pg-kb and the tools kb.* of the platform MCP.

### K `kb`

**Package kb: layer types, LayerDelta, queries, hybrid search** (package, from stage 7). Shared types and pure functions of the knowledge base from stage 7: layers L0 to L5, the LayerDelta as the result of the indexer jobs, the query types of the KnowledgeStore, the hybrid search with RRF and the types of the kb.* tools. No database access and no query implementation (that lives in plugins/pg-kb), no jobs (service indexer).

### K `kb-indexer`

**Package kb-indexer: tree-sitter parser, chunker, delta building** (package, from stage 7). Runs in the sandbox of the indexer jobs L1 and L3: parses repo files with web-tree-sitter, splits them into chunks and builds a LayerDelta from them, called via the command gw-kb-indexer. Never writes to the database and calls no model; planning, acceptance of the delta and embedding belong to the service indexer.

### K `service-standards`

**Standards service: rule metrics with UI page, miner, rule PR, compilation, decay** (service, from stage 7). Measures per rule (rule_id) findings, acceptance and addressed rate, derives rule candidates from accepted feedback, proposes them as a PR on .agents/rules/, compiles confirmed model findings into ast-grep or Opengrep rules with test cases and proposes the withdrawal of weak rules. The only write request is propose_change on .agents/rules/; the service activates no rule itself (merge by CODEOWNERS, auto_activate only at installation level) and loads no guidelines (that is done by @guildwork/guidelines).

### K `service-triage`

**Triage service: duplicates, classification, spam, verifier, auto_close** (service, from stage 7). Classifies new issues without a shell (duplicates and related items with visibility check, labels, assignees, repo, spam and slop, clarity), checks the result deterministically and publishes per property according to configuration; closing only with auto_close and a green T1 gate of the repo. In stage 7 only a single-service run; as the first stage of ticket-to-pr only from stage 9 (FE-1221). The GitHub methods (setLabels, linkItems, closeAsDuplicate) and the executors do not belong here.

### K `driver-blob-gcs`

**BlobStore gcs** (driver, from stage 8). Driver of the BlobStore contract for Google Cloud Storage with signed URLs, versioning and retention per bucket setting, sign-in ambient or via the own issuer (FE-1340). ### K `identitaetsverknuepfung`

**identity_links via OAuth confirmation with a UI page** (role, from stage 8). Links an account of a ticket system (Jira) with an SCM account (GitHub) only through OAuth confirmation of both sides by the user themselves, with the page Link accounts, revocation and audit (FE-1225, FE-1312, FE-1313). Not included: the permission AND check in the router, which only calls resolve, and the base model of the tables identities and identity_links (01).

### K `plugin-exec-k8s`

**ExecutionBackend k8s for Helm operation** (plugin, from stage 8). ExecutionBackend k8s, loaded in the worker pod: sandbox per item as a pod with RuntimeClass in the sandbox namespace, NetworkPolicy per item only to the egress proxy, binding at the proxy via the pod IP (FE-1345, FE-1346). No Docker in the pod, no access to secrets; the Helm chart creates the namespace and the RBAC.

### K `plugin-jira-cloud`

**Jira Cloud: TriggerSource and WorkItemProvider** (plugin, from stage 8). One plugin with the kinds TriggerSource (ingress via admin webhook or automation relay, catch-up via JQL) and WorkItemProvider (read tickets and write them via the Effect Gateway) for Jira Cloud (ADR-09). Not included: identity linking, permission AND check and visibility of ticket targets (control plane) and ADF conversion (@guildwork/adf).

### K `plugin-host`

**Plugin host: trust level, signature, subprocess transport gRPC, distribution as an OCI artifact** (package, from stage 9). Loads plugins and services from signed OCI artifacts with the trust level that the installation assigns, and talks to them via gRPC in a subprocess or in their own container; in addition intake via admin API, CLI and admin UI. Not: starting containers from the control plane (FE-1430), running third-party code in Z0, DB access in the package (intake writes apps/control-plane/src/plugins/third-party.ts).

- Path: `packages/plugin-host/`, package `@guildwork/plugin-host`

### K `plugin-sentry`

**TriggerSource sentry** (plugin, from stage 10). TriggerSource for Seer events from Sentry, mapped to the same event and the same body as incident-handoff; signature headers and fields are unverified and are verified in 10-E03-T02 against documentation and recording. No handoff logic of its own (it lives in incident/intake).

### K `prfixer-modi`

**PR fixer modes dependency_update and ci_doctor** (service, from stage 10). Two modes of the PR fixer as strategies of the same controller: dependency_update repairs red bot update PRs as a stacked PR, manifest and lockfile only via the package manager; ci_doctor finds the cause of red CI on the default branch and keeps updating the same issue. Not for the PR fixer core (11 section 2.4), not for pushes or reruns on the default branch and not for the executor issue (effect catalog).

### K `service-docs`

**Docs service: drift check, docstrings, sync, release** (service, from stage 10). Keeps documentation current without changing code: drift check on PRs (never blocking), docstrings of touched symbols as a follow-up PR, docs PR after merge and release notes as a changelog PR. Not for merges, tags or publications (always done by a human) and not for code changes.
